decisions.reason: We would keep Product A because, having survived its first review in a growing market and fitting closely with our core coolant systems, there is still no sign that its results fall below aspiration levels and our organisational slack supports further commercialization.

We would keep Product C because the nozzle line is a modular complement to our established systems, likely supports broader solution sales, and continued market presence suggests performance is at least acceptable relative to aspirations.

We would keep Product E because it sits directly in our established chip-conveyor portfolio, benefits from our existing engineering and service network, and the earlier pruning of weaker launches lowers the need to withdraw this one now.

We would keep Product F because, although it remains somewhat more uncertain as a close-adjacent launch, no clear aspiration-level failure is visible and a large innovative firm like ours would typically allow more time before reallocating these resources.
